title: release publish runs the tests workflow's whole matrix twice on one commit: the tag push repeats the candidate's green run
body:
`release publish` runs the tests workflow's whole matrix twice on one commit. hv's ruling of 2026-10-29: file it, low, for after tonight, with no build now.

## What happened

- v0.1.18's candidate run 40919937412 passed on a9b8cd7c.
- An hour later, pushing the v0.1.18 tag at that same commit started "Devbin Tests" again, as run 40928750135. molt-vc cancelled it on hv's word.
- The Release workflow (run 40928750466) passed without that run, so the tag run duplicates a verdict already given and costs about an hour of macOS runner.
- CI holds no run from the fast-forward of main to that commit. GitHub lists three runs on a9b8cd7c: the candidate's, 40919937412 (green), the tag's, 40928750135 (cancelled), and Release, 40928750466 (green). A push to main runs Ubuntu and ShellCheck under the workflow's filter, where GitHub starts a run for it at all.

## The trigger lines

In .github/workflows/tests.yml:
- `on.push.tags: ['v[0-9]*', '[0-9]*']` at line 17 starts a run on every release tag.
- `branches: [main, 'candidate/**']` at line 11 starts runs on main and on candidates.
- The macOS and WSL legs, and Test Summary's MACOS_REQUIRED, take `github.ref_type == 'tag'` at :196, :356 and :542, so a tag run carries the whole matrix.

## The ask

Under `release.publish.url`, the candidate run is the gate. So either the workflow does not run on a tag push, or it skips a commit that is already green on its `candidate/<tag>` branch.
- docs/releasing.md's "A publish produces three runs of the tests workflow on one commit" changes with it.
- ci-workflow.bats' trigger arms change with it.
- A project that cuts without a publish repository still needs CI on its tag, so the change must hold for both shapes, or be keyed on whether the project publishes.

---

## Resolution

- A Candidate verdict job runs first in the tests workflow. On a tag it asks release.ci.query's ci-state about `candidate/<tag>` at the tag's commit, and only `green` skips the legs (Ubuntu, macOS, ShellCheck, WSL); `none`, failed, pending, unknown or a failed query run the whole matrix, so a project that cuts without a candidate keeps CI on its tag. Test Summary passes the skips on that green alone and refuses a red verdict job or an unrecognised value. docs/releasing.md, the config's ci.tag note and ci-state's header say so.
- Landed on main at `19d87d30` (cc's bank 0e7becab, validated by vc; its six paths unmoved on main since its base 634bc8e3, so they are the blobs the run tested).
- Evidence: cc's run in slot 01M66HR05738YPP3EMTJY5W2T0: ci-workflow.bats' 7 new and changed arms red at the base (tip 32c1c041, 0 of 7 ok) and green under BSD and GNU; ci-workflow, ci-state, documentation, config and help whole under BSD and GNU, and the tree scans under GNU, all green; critic exit 0.
- The live proof is the next publish: its tag's run should show Candidate verdict green and every leg skipped.
